messages.body_plain:

May I know if its possible perform longitudinal growth modelling  with individual specific time trends using PRS in GenomicSEM?

Thanks in Advance

messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal growth modelling
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajni,
Genomic SEM allows for fitting structural equation models directly to GWAS summary statistics without having to compute PRS. You can use the resulting Genomic SEM model to produce new summary statistics for derived phenotypes, which you can in turn use to compute PRS in raw data (that were not included in the original GWAS summary statistics). If your raw data has longitudinal measurements, then you can certainly model those data using any number of phenotypic longitudinal models (using conventional phenotypic modeling softare, such as HLM, PROC MIXED, lme4, lavaan, OpenMx, MPlus) that incorporate PRS. If you would like to do a "longitudinal" style genetic analysis directly in Genomic SEM, you will need to obtain or otherwise create GWAS summary statistics for different ages or waves of data. The samples do not necessarily need to overlap across ages or waves: i.e. you could obtain GWAS summary statistics for a phenotype from a child sample, and GWAS summary statistics for the same phenotype from an entirely different adolescent sample, and still have information of genetic covariances over time needed for the longitudinal modelling. A growth curve model is only one type of longitudinal-style analysis, and it does have more specialized requirements than other models (e.g. cross-lagged panel models). For instance, a growth curve requires that the exact same measure be obtained at all ages or waves, and further typically also models means over time (which may not be sensible genetic parameters as distinct from phenotypic parameters).
Cheers,
Elliot
